key_insight: The paper establishes a validated way to compute the J-integral in quasicontinuum and finite element settings, including atomistic-to-continuum coupling and quantified uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable crack-driving-force predictions in multiscale fracture simulations, helping engineers model large components while retaining atomistic detail near crack tips.
method: Implemented the J-integral in QC3D using Cauchy-Born-derived stress and strain energy density fields under plane strain.
Validated results against LEFM theory and the virtual crack extension method in three regimes: linear elasticity, nonlinear Cauchy-Born without relaxation, and with atomic relaxation.
Added a Markov chain Monte Carlo framework to estimate uncertainty from mesh and contour/domain choices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with LEFM and VCE across all tested regimes, and a silicon three-point bending simulation where the critical energy release rate matches the Griffith criterion closely.
watch_item: Accuracy still depends on mesh resolution and the chosen integration domain, so the uncertainty quantification must be checked carefully for each model setup.
paper_title: Uncertainty-quantified $J$-integral computation for quasicontinuum and finite element methods
